survey: A red British phone booth, seen three-quarter from slightly above. The near corner post faces the viewer. The narrower left side recedes to the left and the wider front door face recedes to the right. Below, the booth stands on a purple plinth whose top surface is visible from above. Its bottom edges rise to the left on the side face and to the right on the front face, so it reads as resting flat on the green floor. The window bars (3 columns on each face) sit inside frames that follow their face. Bars near the top run almost level and bars lower down slope more, matching the plinth edges, which is correct for a camera above the booth. All verticals stay vertical, as the red marks on the tool sheet show, which is acceptable stylisation. A cornice band wraps both faces at the same height. Above it, each face has an arched sign panel with a gold crown, under a domed roof whose top is seen from above, matching the plinth. The handle sticks out from the front door toward the viewer. A blue payphone hangs on the back wall, seen through the front glass and facing the same way as the front face. Overall the booth and its ground are seen from one camera, and the parallel edges on each face converge gradually toward one side.
